'''''Acer tataricum''''', the '''Tatar maple''' or '''Tatarian maple''', is a species of [[maple]] widespread across central and southeastern [[Europe]] and temperate [[Asia]], from [[Austria]] and [[Turkey]], and in some circumscriptions, with a disjunct population in eastern Asia in northern and central [[China]], [[Japan]] and the [[Russian Far East]]. The species is named after the [[Tatars|Tatar peoples]] of southern Russia; the tree's name is similarly commonly also misspelled "Tartar" or "Tartarian" in English.<ref name=rushforth>{{cite book|author=Rushforth, K.|year=1999|title=''Trees of Britain and Europe''|publisher=[[HarperCollins|Collins]]|isbn=978-0-00-220013-4}}</ref><ref name=ecosystema>Ecosystema: [http://www.ecosystema.ru/08nature/trees/42.htm ''Acer tataricum''] (in Russian; [https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ru&u=http://www.ecosystema.ru/08nature/trees/42.htm&sa=X&oi=translate& google translation])</ref>

==Description==
''Acer tataricum'' is a [[deciduous]] spreading [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to {{convert|4|-|12|m}} tall, with a short trunk up to {{convert|20|-|50|cm}} diameter and slender branches. The [[Bark (botany)|bark]] is thin, pale brown, and smooth at first but becoming shallowly fissured on old plants. The [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite and simple, broadly ovate, {{convert|4.5|-|10|cm}} long and {{convert|3|-|7|cm}} broad, unlobed or with three or five shallow lobes, and matt green above; the leaf margin is coarsely and irregularly toothed; the leaf petiole is slender, often pink-tinged, {{convert|2|-|5|cm}} long. The [[flower]]s are whitish-green, {{convert|5|-|8|mm}} diameter, produced in spreading panicles in spring as the leaves open. The [[fruit]] is a paired reddish [[samara (fruit)|samara]], {{convert|10|-|12|mm}} long with a {{convert|2|-|3|cm}} wing, maturing in late summer to early autumn.<ref name=rushforth/><ref name=ecosystema/><ref name=o>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=250084117 Flora of China, ''Acer tataricum'' Linnaeus, 1753.  <big>鞑靼槭</big> da da qi ]</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
Subspecies accepted by [[the Plant List]] maintained by [[Kew Gardens]] in London:<ref name=o/><ref name=POWO/>
*''Acer tataricum'' subsp. ''aidzuense'' <small>(Franch.) P.C.DeJong </small>. Japan. Included in Amur maple when that is treated as a separate species.
*[[Acer tataricum subsp. ginnala|''Acer tataricum'' subsp. ''ginnala'']] <small>(Maxim.) Wesm.</small> (Amur maple, syn. ''Acer ginnala''). Korea, easternmost Mongolia, eastern Russia, northeastern China
*''Acer tataricum'' subsp. ''semenovii'' <small>(Regel & Herder) A.E.Murray</small> - Central Asia in Afghanistan, southern Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, westernmost Tibet
*''Acer tataricum'' subsp. ''tataricum'' - Caucasus, Turkey, Austria, Bulgaria, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Ukraine, Iran
*''Acer tataricum'' subsp. ''theiferum'' <small>(W.P.Fang) Y.S.Chen & P.C.de Jong</small> - eastern China. Included in Amur maple when that is treated as a separate species.

Some botanists treat ''Acer tataricum'' subsp. ''ginnala'' as a separate species ''Acer ginnala''.<ref name=EuroMed>{{cite web | title=Acer ginnala | website=Euro+Med-Plantbase | url=https://europlusmed.org/cdm_dataportal/taxon/bb88dff3-1091-4a1a-a8a7-bbcf5b522e3a | access-date=2024-10-18}}</ref><ref name=rushforth/><ref name=usdaG>{{PLANTS|symbol=ACGI|taxon=Acer ginnala|access-date=2024-10-18}}</ref> The two differ conspicuously in the glossy, deeply lobed leaves of ''A. ginnala'', compared to the matt, unlobed or only shallowly lobed leaves of ''A. tataricum'', and are separated by a roughly 3,000 km range gap.<ref name=rushforth/>

==Cultivation and uses==
[[File:Acer tataricum.jpg|thumb|200x200px|Tatar maple cultivated near the central railway station in Helsinki, Finland.]]
Tatar maple is occasionally grown as an ornamental plant in gardens throughout Europe and also in North America.<ref name=rushforth/> In Russia, it is valued in farmland [[shelterbelt]]s.<ref name=ecosystema/> It is locally [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] and sometimes invasive in eastern North America.<ref name=usdaT>{{PLANTS|symbol=ACTA80|taxon=Acer tataricum|access-date=2024-10-18}}</ref><ref name="o829">{{cite web | title=Amur maple (Acer ginnala) and Tatarian maple (Acer tataricum) | website=Minnesota Department of Natural Resources | date=2018-10-19 | url=https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/invasives/terrestrialplants/woody/amurmaple.html | access-date=2024-10-18}}</ref>
